rules.quote: Don’t add full stops to the ends of headings, page headers, footers or captions.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop at the end of a heading, page header, footer, or caption
rules.why: G-1: Specific actionable instruction within list of minimal punctuation rules.

rules.quote: Don’t use a semicolon at the end of each item in a bullet list.
rules.violation_condition: a semicolon at the end of an item in a bullet list
rules.why: G-1: Specific rule for bullet list punctuation.

rules.quote: Unless each item is a full sentence or the last item in a list, don’t use a full stop for items in bullet lists.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop at the end of a bullet list item that is not a full sentence and not the last item in the list
when: item is a full sentence
item is the last item in a list
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Rule on full stops in bullet list items with stated exceptions.

rules.quote: Don’t use full stops between letters in an acronym or initialism.
rules.violation_condition: full stops between letters in an acronym or initialism
rules.why: G-1: Distinct rule on punctuation inside acronyms/initialisms.

rules.quote: Don’t use a full stop at the end of most abbreviations.
rules.specification: Abbreviations generally do not take terminal full stops in Australian government style, except as specified in the abbreviations topic.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop at the end of an abbreviation that does not require one
rules.why: G-1, E-4: Specific rule on full stops in abbreviations.

covers.quote: Check each document for double and multiple spaces and delete them.

rules.quote: Include a single space after a punctuation mark at the end of a sentence. Never use double spaces.
rules.violation_condition: double or multiple spaces following a sentence-ending punctuation mark
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Sentence states rule and absorbs advice sentence in the same block.

covers.quote: Capitalise the first word in a sentence and in headings
opening quoted speech within a sentence

rules.quote: Capitalise the first word in a sentence. Use lower case for all other words, unless those words include proper nouns.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence starting with a lowercase letter, or sentence words that are not proper nouns starting with a capital letter
when: words include proper nouns
opening quoted speech within a sentence
rules.why: G-4: Rule covering sentence case for sentences and quoted speech.

covers.quote: Capitalise the first word in a sentence and in headings

rules.specification: Use sentence case for headings (capitalise the first word and proper nouns only).
rules.violation_condition: a heading not written in sentence case
rules.why: G-1: Distinct rule specifically governing headings.

rules.quote: Do not use all capitals for headings, unless the visual design for the content meets WCAG in all respects.
rules.specification: Headings must not be written in all-capital letters.
rules.violation_condition: a heading written in ALL CAPS without WCAG conformance verification
when: visual design meets WCAG in all respects
rules.why: G-2, G-3: Direct prohibition with WCAG exception.

rules.quote: Use sentence case with italics for titles of works mentioned in the content.
rules.violation_condition: a title of a work mentioned in content that is not in sentence case or not italicised
when: reference is included in a heading within the content
rules.why: G-1: Explicit rule for styling titles of works.

examples.note: Spelt-out proper noun uses initial capitals

parts.quote: ‘NSW’ is written out as ‘New South Wales’.

rules.quote: If the shortened form represents a proper noun, start each word with a capital letter.
rules.violation_condition: the spelt-out form of a shortened proper noun written without initial capital letters
when: shortened form represents a proper noun
rules.why: G-1: Clear prescriptive rule for spelling out shortened proper nouns.

covers.quote: The spelt-out form might not need initial capitals, even if an acronym or initialism has them.

examples.note: Common noun initialism spelt out in lower case

parts.quote: ‘EIS’ is written out as ‘environmental impact statement’.

examples.note: Common noun initialism spelt out in lower case

rules.quote: If the shortened form represents a common noun, do not begin each word of the full form with a capital letter.
rules.violation_condition: the spelt-out form of a shortened common noun written with initial capital letters
when: shortened form represents a common noun
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Rule on capitalisation of common noun shortened forms.

rules.quote: Only use capitals when the style is standardised or specified in regulations, for symbols of units of measurement.
rules.specification: Unit symbols must be lower case unless capitalisation is specified by standard SI conventions or regulations.
rules.violation_condition: a symbol for a unit of measurement written with capitals when not standardised or specified in regulations
when: style is standardised or specified in regulations
rules.why: G-1: Specific rule on unit of measurement symbols.

covers.quote: This includes titles for executives specified in legislation.

parts.quote: Chief Defence Scientist Tanya Monro presented the award ...

rules.quote: Use capitals when an official title precedes the name of the office holder.
rules.violation_condition: an official title preceding the name of the office holder written in lower case
when: official title precedes the name of the office holder
official title includes executives specified in legislation
rules.why: G-1: Distinct rule governing titles preceding personal names.

covers.quote: You do not need to use capitals when the title is an organisational name given to an office holder.

parts.quote: The Senior Policy Adviser offered their view ...

rules.quote: Unless advised in this manual, avoid using capitals in body text for a particular position or role within an organisation.
rules.specification: Do not capitalise job titles or organisational roles in body text when they appear without a personal name.
rules.violation_condition: a position or role within an organisation capitalised in body text when not preceding a name
when: not advised otherwise in this manual
rules.why: G-1, G-3: Rule against capitalising positions/roles in body text.
